conviction_note: The Q3 print is noise next to a solvency event already under way: the operating subsidiary filed for bankruptcy on 27 Nov at 13:00 UTC, lessors terminated all 12 aircraft leases, wages are unpaid, and the listed parent says 'alternatives are being considered involving the Company', so the window most likely carries a parent insolvency step or nothing decisive, with a takeover-rescue lottery as the upside tail; abs_move 45 on 3-session moves of -85/-13/-59%, p_up 33 because equity ranks behind a USD 52m 15% senior secured bond and the lessors, while retail lottery flow and a possible suspension (a zero move) keep it off the extremes. The scaled -15.3 and the findings' sum of -13 agree in sign and size; that is coincidence, not fitting.

findings.finding: The listed parent's own solvency is unresolved and its 27 Nov release signals that it is next: the operating subsidiary is bankrupt, all 12 leases are terminated, November wages went unpaid, and 'alternatives are currently being considered involving the Company and selected subsidiaries', so a parent insolvency or restructuring step that wipes or dilutes equity is the likeliest decisive news inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Solvency news in this run: -85% on 25 Nov (critical-financing release), -13% on 26 Nov (suspension of flights), about -59% intraday 27 Nov (lease terminations and subsidiary bankruptcy); the July 2024 trading update moved -43%.
findings.original_quote: Lønnen som skulle vært utbetalt onsdag, uteble. (e24, 26 Nov: 'The salary that should have been paid on Wednesday did not arrive.') Release itself in English: 'alternatives are currently being considered involving the Company and selected subsidiaries.'
findings.why_not_priced: The Friday-close price (~0.011 NOK) still values the equity above zero and is set by retail flow in a Recovery Box; if the parent's insolvency were priced the stock would be suspended or trading at the tick floor. English wires had not reported the subsidiary bankruptcy at the time of the search; only Norwegian press (e24) had.
findings.independence: e24 reports unpaid wages and the pilots' union confirming it, a different source from the company releases: https://e24.no/i/5309R6/norse-har-ikke-betalt-loenn-til-ansatte ; lease terminations reported separately by e24: https://e24.no/i/0vn29B/norse-leasingselskaper-avslutter-leieavtaler-for-alle-selskapets-fly

findings.finding: Upside tail: the company is in talks with investors about a takeover that 'would include a financing solution', JP Morgan is engaged, and the parent and its UK subsidiary (which e24 says operates the last five aircraft) are 'working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations'; any announced deal in the window would pop a lottery-priced stock, but equity ranks behind the USD 52m 15% senior secured bond and the lessors.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Strategic-review/takeover headlines earlier in 2026 did not lift the stock durably; the 9 Nov session ran +10% intraday on volume with no release; the June 2026 rights issue and bond conversion closed -5.8%.
findings.original_quote: e24: 'investeringsbanken JP Morgan er engasjert for å finne strategiske løsninger' (the investment bank JP Morgan has been engaged to find strategic solutions)
findings.why_not_priced: A rescue would be new information; the price holds a small option on it, not the outcome. Sized small because the money in any deal goes to the secured bond, the lessors and the bankrupt estate before the ASA shareholders; the 27 Nov release talks about preserving value for 'involved stakeholders', not shareholders.
findings.independence: e24 on JP Morgan engagement and takeover talks: https://e24.no/i/5309R6/norse-har-ikke-betalt-loenn-til-ansatte ; e24 on the UK subsidiary continuing: https://e24.no/i/mMRJB4/flyselskapet-norse-slaar-driftsselskap-konkurs

findings.finding: The Q3 report scheduled for 30 Nov (calendar published 20 Nov, before the collapse) will, if it comes, carry accounts for a business that has since lost its operating company and fleet, likely with going-concern language and impairments; if it is postponed, that is itself a sign that the parent is heading for a filing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Results days: -22% (Q4 2023), -21% (Q2 2024), +9% (Q3 2024), -6.6% (Q2 2025); median 3.9% across 13 announcement days.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the collapse makes Q3 numbers secondary (lesson: in a live bid or solvency event, results are noise). What is unpriced is only whether the report formally confirms the parent cannot continue.

outside_window.finding: Outcome of the bankruptcy estate's handling of the Norwegian subsidiary and the lessors' repossession of the 12 aircraft (contested terminations); trustee appointed by Agder District Court
